start_here: Say to your AI: "Write a word template for my 2.5 second opening line: Meet the, then the baker as a slot, who rose early, then Two days ago as a slot." It runs tool:write-a-word-template-from-the-words-i-keep-and-the-slots.

lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON. For this folder the account row holds your own dimensions registry.
alike: a config sheet or settings spreadsheet
a notes page of defaults per project

instructions: 1. Write a request file, for example bakery/parts-request.json: {"out": folder, "dim": "speech.word", "templates": [{"name","t0","t1","source","parts","slots"}]}. A kept part is ["K","words"]; a slot part is ["S","SLOTNAME","the words in it"]; slots maps each name to [type, note].

2. Say to your AI: "Write the word template from bakery/parts-request.json". It reads the row with tools:list and runs python3 -I tools/fill-a-template-without-changing-its-words/do-work/token_table_from_parts.py --request bakery/parts-request.json
3. Read the last line: {"result":{"written":[{"file","tokens","slots"}]}} lists each template written; {"error": ...} says what to change (for example a slot part naming a slot that is not in slots).
4. Take the template to tool:fill-a-word-template, then judge rewrites with tool:check-words-against-a-word-template.
5. Keep your own words, slots and ids in a list:settings row and pass it as settings_record in the request; never write them into the tool's folder.

worked_examples.title: An opening line with a person slot and a time slot
worked_examples.ask: Write a word template for my opening line.
worked_examples.given: From tools/fill-a-template-without-changing-its-words/test/test_token_table_from_parts.py (its made-up parts) run for real: bakery/parts-request.json is {"out":"bakery/templates","dim":"speech.word","templates":[{"name":"open-line","t0":1.5,"t1":4.0,"source":"bakery/voice-notes.txt","parts":[["K","Meet the"],["S","WHO","baker, Sam Example"],["K","who rose early."],["S","WHEN","Two days ago."]],"slots":{"WHO":["PERSON","who the line is about"],"WHEN":["TIME","how long ago"]}}]}. Command: python3 -I tools/fill-a-template-without-changing-its-words/do-work/token_table_from_parts.py --request bakery/parts-request.json
worked_examples.hands_back: Exit 0 and the last line {"result": {"written": [{"file": "bakery/templates/open-line.template.json", "tokens": 11, "slots": 2}]}}. The 11 words are KEEP or SLOT in order (Meet the | baker, Sam Example | who rose early. | Two days ago.); slots WHO (PERSON) and WHEN (TIME) are listed with rule "hand".

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for tool settings and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and list:settings as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
